children: , the memory and storage chipmaker, faced a new test from Chinese rival CXMT as its latest DRAM platform entered mass production. Micron shares rose about 0.4% to $1,084.87 at 10.31am ET time on Friday, September 25. The stock also stood 66.81% above its $650.37 GF Value estimate. Investors are paying a steep premium for Micron's prospects even as another supplier adds capacity.

CXMT says its new LPDDR5X chips hold 24 gigabits each, 50% more than its previous comparable products. It also claims at least 50% more gross chips per wafer. As Reuters reported, the chips are aimed at smartphones and other portable devices. Those production figures are a warning for rivals, but they do not yet show how many usable chips CXMT can deliver or how quickly customers will adopt them.

For Micron, the nearer risk is tougher pricing in mobile DRAM. Its high-bandwidth memory business gives it a different source of demand from AI customers, but a richer product mix cannot shield every part of the company from new supply. With the shares priced well above GF Value, investors will want proof that premium memory sales can keep growing if conventional DRAM prices soften.

title: Micron Stocks Gain While CXMT Raises the Commodity Threat
